Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

3. The present appeal preferred by the insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988,
seeks to assail the order dated 14.11.2022 passed by the learned MACT, insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned.
4. In support of the appeal, learned counsel for the appellant has raised two primary contentions.

The first and foremost being that even though it was the claimant's own statement before the police authorities, at the time of lodging of FIR in respect of the accident, that he was unemployed, the learned Tribunal has erroneously presumed that he was working as an electrician.
He also contends that the learned Tribunal has further erred in presuming that permanent disability of 28% in his left leg had to be treated as his functional disability as well.

He next contends that once the doctors were unable to testify regarding the functional disability of the claimant, the learned Tribunal could not have taken the onus on itself and come to the conclusion that the permanent disability in his lower left limb could be taken as his functional disability.

5. This Court is prima facie not inclined to agree with this plea of the appellant that merely because the concerned doctor was not in a position to give any conclusive opinion regarding the functional The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Devender Kumar Sharma & Ors on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154493023/
1 disability of the appellant, the learned Tribunal also could not have come to any conclusion on that count.
6.

sentences.text: However, taking into account the appellant's plea that no evidence had been led before the learned Tribunal to show that the respondent was working as an electrician, upon the appellant taking steps, issue notice to respondent no.1 through all permissible modes.

7. Taking into account that no recovery rights against the owner and driver of the offending vehicle have been granted under the impugned award, no notice is required to be issued to respondent nos.2 & 3.
8.
This is an application filed by the appellant seeking stay of the impugned award during the pendency of the present appeal.

10. Taking into account that the appellant is only assailing the quantum of compensation, the application is disposed of by directing the appellant to deposit, within six weeks, 75% of the awarded amount with the learned Tribunal with a further direction to the learned Tribunal to release the same in favour of the claimant as per the disbursal scheme contained in the impugned award.
